title: removeStopWords
summary: Remove stop words from tokenized documents.

gpu_support.notes: `removeStopWords` filters host text metadata and does not use provider kernels.

description: `removeStopWords(documents)` removes stop words from RunMat `tokenizedDocument` compatibility objects using the object's language metadata and the same compatibility lists returned by `stopWords`.
behaviors: `documents` must be a RunMat `tokenizedDocument` object created by `tokenizedDocument`.
Numeric and resident tensor inputs, including every integer class, are not text documents and reject before provider access rather than being gathered or converted to text.
`removeStopWords(documents,'IgnoreCase',false)` removes only tokens that match the stop-word list case exactly.
The result preserves `Shape`, `TokenizeMethod`, and `Language` metadata while recomputing document lengths and vocabulary.
RunMat removes stop words from derived `letters` and `other` token types. Punctuation, URLs, hashtags, mentions, and emoticons are preserved by this helper.

English and German tokenized documents are supported by RunMat's current tokenizer. Japanese and Korean stop-word lists exist for `stopWords`, but MeCab-backed Japanese/Korean tokenized-document support remains tracked by the broader Text Analytics compatibility issue.

examples.input:
documents = tokenizedDocument(["an example of a short sentence"; "a second short sentence"]);
newDocuments = removeStopWords(documents)
examples.output: `newDocuments` contains `example short sentence` and `second short sentence`.

faqs.question: Does `removeStopWords` support raw strings?
faqs.answer: No. Convert raw text with `tokenizedDocument` first.

faqs.question: Can I provide a custom word list?
faqs.answer: No. Use of custom lists belongs to `removeWords`, which remains tracked by the broader Text Analytics compatibility issue.

faqs.question: Does `removeStopWords` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. It filters host text metadata and has no `runmat-accelerate` provider path.

points: `IgnoreCase` must be a logical scalar; the default is `true`.
The document object's `Language` metadata selects the stop-word list.

gpu_residency: `removeStopWords` filters host text metadata and has no provider kernel.
